summary: Tree tower on Tannery Hill, Tioga County PA, built 1914 and no longer standing; no source found describing the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower is no longer standing; no removal date found

access.note: The hill lies in Tioga State Forest and the Mid State Trail climbs it; no source describes the tower site itself

visit.trail_note: Mid State Trail ascent; camping off-trail permitted under state forest rules

evidence.supports: Tree tower built 1914, still used circa 1917, no longer standing
evidence.quote: This tree tower was built in 1914, was still used circa 1917 and is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: Hill in Tioga State Forest near Morris
evidence.quote: The Tannery Hill Hike at Tioga State Forest near Morris, Pennsylvania is a moderate 5.8-mile out-and-back hike

evidence.supports: Mid State Trail climbs the hill
evidence.quote: Hikers will follow the Mid State Trail as it begins the moderate mountain ascent

evidence.supports: Camping off-trail allowed under state forest rules
evidence.quote: Backpacking and camping is permitted off-trail here, but campers must follow all state forest rules and regulations.

evidence.supports: Trail crosses the back of the hill along a plateau
evidence.quote: the trail will flatten out as it undulates its way across the backside of Tannery Hill along a plateau

evidence.supports: No defined campsites as of July 2023
evidence.quote: Note that as of July, 2023 there were no defined campsites along the trail

evidence.supports: Trail begins at a small parking turnout on Stony Fork Road
evidence.quote: This hike begins along Stony Fork Rd just north of the junction with Clay Mind Rd in a small parking turnout for the Mid State Trail.

sources.title: Tannery Hill Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register (FFLOS US 504)

notes_for_editor: Only the FFLOS register entry speaks to the tower (tree tower, built 1914, still used circa 1917, no longer standing). MyHikes supports only the trail context on the hill. Two searches found no staffing, fire, or removal-date source, and no other record for the tower. Brief record (Tioga County, registered 2008) matches the register and map data. Story is short because the evidence is thin.
